principles: Every number/artifact has a committed deterministic producer.
Fingerprint match is over an explicit frozen domain (flags + numeric predicates), never the whole verify result.
Two-pronged viability: fail-closed only if the fingerprint carries a real failure signal; accept-only self-consistent variant goes to the acceptance bucket.
Instrument is read/called only, never modified; mutations in mkdtemp isolation.
Freeze before scored runs: protocol.json + sha256 is the contract M1-M4 read.
drivers: The plan (B-e86f) is a frozen pre-registration; protocol.json must match section 6.1/7.
verify has no textual reason field, forcing fingerprint-based adjudication.
The full-profile 1M run is the only heavy compute — measure once.

options.name: hand-author-fingerprints-from-source-reading
cons: Risks a no-op class like rev-1 seed-swap

rationale: Plan mandates every class demonstrably viability-checked; the spike proved it on real verify output (15 fail-closed, 2 accepted). Hand-authoring risks the rev-1 seed-swap no-op and cannot honestly disposition accept-only variants.

preMortem.trigger: row-reorder or byte-flip picks different indices across runs
preMortem.consequence: frozen fingerprint is not reproducible; freeze meaningless
preMortem.mitigation: fix mutation indices/inputs as constants so every run mutates identically

preMortem.trigger: protocol.json key ordering or floating rates differ across runs
preMortem.mitigation: canonical JSON serialization + exact/integer predicate encoding

preMortem.trigger: 1M generate+verify OOMs or exceeds a sane time budget
preMortem.consequence: cost calibration and full-N cannot be finalized
preMortem.mitigation: capture elapsed/rss, record a budget_cap honestly; record the stop rather than fake a number
